title: Gatekeeper for staged routing policy rollouts and dynamic fallback selectors
creator: Sarah Nguyen
description: Build a 'gatekeeper' layer inside the policy engine that validates, stages, and enforces safe rollouts for routing configs. The feature combines schema-level checks for new routing selectors (region weighting, tier affinity, model-variant fallbacks) with runtime heuristics that prevent misconfigurations from causing large-scale traffic loss or region starvation. Core capabilities: 1) Pre-apply validation: extended DSL checks that verify scoring expressions, percent allocations, and cross-field invariants (sum-of-weights, mutual exclusivity, fallback chain termination). 2) Staged enablement: support rollout windows and percent-based canaries that the console can toggle; the gatekeeper ensures staged configs are applied incrementally and can be automatically paused if SLO regressions are detected. 3) Dynamic fallback selectors: allow policy authors to declare fallback model variants with scoring rules (latency, cost, quality tiers). Gatekeeper will compute and expose the chosen fallback chain and validate that every request has a bounded fallback path. 4) Safety circuits: enforce limits such as per-region min-capacity, max-fallback-depth, and global-cost-guardrails; provide an emergency-override that routes to a verified baseline model if constraints are violated. 5) Observability hooks: emit structured events for rollout steps, validation failures, and circuit trips for Console dashboards and alerting.
comments: 2026-03-01: Kickoff meeting — scoped MVP: pre-apply validation + percent canary + simple two-level fallback chains. Decided to defer advanced scoring language until follow-up.
2026-03-03: Design review with Product & Console — agreed on gating signals: 95th latency, error-rate, and token-cost variance for auto-pause. Mateo to prototype enforcement API by 2026-03-10.

2026-03-05: Spike completed — implemented an in-memory sampler to simulate percent-based rollouts and verified distribution across regions; found an edge-case where zero-weight entries were not trimmed leading to division-by-zero in earlier impl.

2026-03-07: Security review requested — gatekeeper will read rollout metadata and emit audit events; added scoped KMS permission check for private deployments. Security asked for explicit allowlist for emergency-override operators.

2026-03-09: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/policy-engine/pull/612 — includes DSL grammar extension, schema tests, and gatekeeper smoke harness. Requesting review from @anna-l and @david-k for runtime safety checks.

2026-03-10: Perf run on canary harness — added microbenchmark showing ~3% CPU overhead at 10k rps with default cache enabled. Decided to add a lightweight fast-path that bypasses full validation for known-stable configs.
Follow-ups: add rich Console UI for staged rollout visualization, integrate with alerts on canary regressions, and extend DSL to express latency vs cost tradeoff weights.
